name: Non-Specific Neck Pain
description: 4-phase program: Pain relief, motor control, strengthening, functional integration
pain_rule: Max. 3/10 pain during exercises. Reduce load if pain increases.
evidence_base: Gross et al. (2015): Exercise for mechanical neck disorders
Jull et al. (2008): Cranio-cervical flexion training
Falla et al. (2012): Specific deep cervical flexor exercise
progression_criteria: Phase 1 to 2: 7 days, min. 4 sessions, avg. pain ≤ 3/10
Phase 2 to 3: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, avg. pain ≤ 3/10
Phase 3 to 4: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, avg. pain ≤ 3/10

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Acute Pain Relief**

In this phase, the focus is on gentle mobilization and activation of the deep neck muscles. Your neck is sensitive, but movement is the best medicine.

**Goal:** Pain reduction and initial habituation to controlled movement.

**Strategy:**
- Gentle movements within the pain-free range
- Activation of the deep neck flexors (Chin Tuck)
- Stretching of tight muscles (upper trapezius)
- Frequent, short sessions rather than long ones

**Scientific basis:** Early, pain-adapted mobilization leads to better outcomes than rest (Gross et al., 2015). The deep neck flexors are often inhibited in neck pain and need to be specifically targeted.
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Motor Control**

You have made it through the acute phase! Now we train the precision of your neck movements. The deep neck flexors and scapula stabilizers are the focus.

**Goal:** Improved neuromuscular control and postural stability.

**Strategy:**
- Cranio-cervical flexion (CCF) to activate the deep neck flexors
- Scapula control for stable shoulder blades
- Quality over quantity — precision matters more than repetition count
- Progressive increase of hold times

**Scientific basis:** The CCF training method by Jull et al. (2008) is the gold standard for deep neck flexor rehabilitation. Deficits in motor control are a key factor in chronic neck pain.
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Progressive Strengthening**

Your control has improved. Now we increase the load — isometrically and dynamically. The neck becomes more resilient.

**Goal:** Building strength and resilience in the neck-shoulder region.

**Strategy:**
- Isometric exercises in 4 directions against hand resistance
- Dynamic resistance band training for scapula stability
- Progressive weight increase (shrugs)
- Transition from controlled to loaded movement

**Scientific basis:** Progressive strengthening of the cervical-scapulothoracic muscles significantly reduces neck pain and disability (O'Leary et al., 2012). The combination of isometric and dynamic training shows the best long-term results.
phase_education.4:
**Phase 4: Functional Integration**

You're almost there! In this phase, we prepare your neck for full everyday loading — carrying, lifting, sport.

**Goal:** Full resilience and return to normal activity.

**Strategy:**
- Functional whole-body exercises with neck loading
- Farmer Walk for postural control under load
- Overhead movements for full shoulder chain resilience
- Sport-/work-specific load tests

**Scientific basis:** Integrating the neck into whole-body movements is critical for transfer to daily life. Loaded exercises stimulate tissue adaptation and build confidence in one's own resilience.

exercises.name: Chin Tuck
exercises.description: Gently retract the chin toward the neck to activate the deep neck flexors. Sit upright, eyes forward.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and gentle mobilization

exercises.name: Gentle Neck Rotation
exercises.description: Slowly turn the head left and right to the pain-free endpoint. No fast movements.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and gentle mobilization

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.description: Tilt the head sideways, consciously pull the opposite shoulder down. Gentle stretch along the side of the neck.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and gentle mobilization

exercises.name: Cranio-Cervical Flexion (CCF)
exercises.description: Supine, head on pillow. Slowly and controlled move the chin toward the chest — deep neck flexor activation.
exercises.phase_goal: Deep neck flexor activation and scapula stability

exercises.name: Scapula Retraction
exercises.description: Squeeze shoulder blades together and hold. Shoulders stay down. Upright posture.
exercises.phase_goal: Deep neck flexor activation and scapula stability

exercises.name: Prone Chin Tuck
exercises.description: In prone: tuck the chin and gently lift the head. Strengthens the deep neck extensors.
exercises.phase_goal: Deep neck flexor activation and scapula stability

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Exercise (4 Directions)
exercises.description: Hand resistance against the head in flexion, extension, lateral flexion left/right. Hold without moving.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening

exercises.name: Resistance Band Rows
exercises.description: Resistance band anchored in front, pull elbows back. Shoulder blades together. Strengthens mid-trapezius and rhomboids.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening

exercises.name: Weighted Shrugs
exercises.description: With dumbbells, pull shoulders up and lower with control. Upper trapezius strengthening.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening

exercises.name: Farmer Walk (Loaded Carry)
exercises.description: Carry heavy dumbbells and walk upright. Trains postural control under load.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific loading and return to activity

exercises.name: Push-Up Plus
exercises.description: Push-up with additional protraction of the shoulder blades at the top. Serratus anterior activation.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific loading and return to activity

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.description: Shoulder press with dumbbells. Trains the full shoulder chain and postural control.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific loading and return to activity

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing With Neck Relaxation
exercises.description: Supine, hands on belly. Breathe deeply into the abdomen, consciously release the neck muscles with each exhale.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and gentle mobilization

exercises.name: Supported Chin Tuck (With Towel)
exercises.description: Supine with rolled towel under the neck. Minimally tuck the chin, towel provides feedback and support.
exercises.phase_goal: Deep neck flexor activation and scapula stability

exercises.name: Light Isometrics (2 Directions)
exercises.description: Only flexion and extension against light hand resistance. No lateral pressure. Build up slowly.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening

exercises.name: Light Carry (Grocery Bags)
exercises.description: Light weights (2–4 kg per hand), carry and walk upright. Control posture, stop if symptoms arise.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific loading and return to activity

exercises.name: Active Neck Rotation (Full Range)
exercises.description: Slow, controlled head rotation left and right to the full pain-free endpoint. Consciously move past the midline.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and gentle mobilization

exercises.name: Dynamic CCF With Progression
exercises.description: CCF training with increasing pressure levels (22, 24, 26, 28, 30 mmHg). Hold and release with control.
exercises.intensity: Progressive — aim for the next level
exercises.phase_goal: Deep neck flexor activation and scapula stability

exercises.name: Heavy Shrugs (Barbell)
exercises.description: With barbell or heavy dumbbells. Shrug shoulders maximally, hold 2 sec, lower with control.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening

exercises.name: 6-Direction Neck Mobility
exercises.description: Flexion, extension, lateral flexion L/R, rotation L/R — full ROM with control. Combine in circles at the end.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific loading and return to activity

exercises.name: Active Neck Rotation (Mid Range)
exercises.description: Seated: slowly turn the head left and right, up to 75% of the pain-free range. Deliberate and controlled.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and gentle mobilization

exercises.name: CCF Training (Standard)
exercises.description: Supine with stabilizer: chin tuck against 22–26 mmHg. Hold 10 seconds, release with control. Moderate progression.
exercises.phase_goal: Deep neck flexor activation and scapula stability

exercises.name: Isometrics 4 Directions (Moderate)
exercises.description: Flexion, extension, lateral flexion L/R against hand resistance. Moderate intensity, all 4 directions.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening

exercises.name: Farmer Walk (Moderate)
exercises.description: Moderate weights (6–10 kg per hand), carry and walk. 30 seconds, control posture. Pause if symptoms arise.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-/work-specific loading and return to activity
